title: ספייקי

spec.palette: designed ramps, at most 5 steps each: olive 5, brass 5, teal 4, glass 3, smoke 2, ivory 2, red 1, mark 1

source: hand-placed pixels at 0 deg, every column (tools/art_host/weapons/guided_px.py); rows turned RotSprite-style (Scale2x x3, nearest), stray pixels out, a 1 px outline; the mark upright in the overlay only
character:
WHO: a shoulder launcher stitched from three tubes: a flared TEAL exhaust bell at the back, a scratched OLIVE middle with
       a taped label plate, a BRASS front with rings; a box sight with a glowing orange lens on top; a pistol grip wrapped in
       ivory tape with a GAME-PAD (d-pad, a red and a green button) where the trigger guard should be; the next missile
       sits in the mouth, its fins outside, a camera EYE in its nose. You steer it like a video game.
  IDLE: the missile is curious: it peeks a little out of the tube, looks round with its nose camera, glances back at the
        hero and ducks in again; the sight's lens blinks now and then. FIRE: tick 0 the missile leaves, a back-blast roars
        out of the bell behind him, the whole tube kicks; at 6 the remote comes up: an antenna pops out of the sight and the
        lens turns green (he is steering); then the RELOAD JOKE: the next missile pops into the mouth like toast on a spring,
        overshoots, bounces back and settles, glancing at him.
cell_note: a bigger cell than the contract's 64: it holds the weapon at every angle with its moving parts thrown out and the toss

equip.note: 18 ticks: up from the hip with a dark sight; at 8 the SCREEN comes on: the lens flickers bright and settles orange: ready

idle.note: 2.4 s: the missile is curious: it peeks out of the tube a pixel, two, looks round with its nose camera, glances back at the hero, ducks in; the sight's lens blinks once

fire.note: 40 ticks = the cooldown. Tick 0 the shot: the missile leaves the mouth (FX's, from `muzzle`) with a small flash and the whole tube kicks back and up; a ring of smoke puffs from the mouth (no back-blast: the bell sits at his chin, critic 18.11). At 6 the REMOTE comes up: an antenna pops out of the sight and the lens turns green (he is steering; its tip blinks red). At 26 the RELOAD JOKE: the next missile pops into the mouth like toast on a spring, overshoots, bounces back a pixel too far, settles and glances back at him

empty.note: 12 ticks: the click on an empty tube (the lens dims, no missile pops), a droop; at 6 he tosses it away in front of him, nose down, the tag trailing

catch.note: the hand-off from the unarmed catch (catch.json has the body's frames): it lands dark in his hands, the sight wakes, the missile peeks; the reveal from the last frame

aim_note: a frame's aim = degrees the weapon turns from its rest (the idle's first frame is 0), added to the body's aim; kick = [px along the barrel (negative = back), px up, degrees up]
mark: the made-in-Israel mark as a SMALL HANGING TAG (the beta's pattern: the tube has no calm 13 x 13 place): an ivory luggage tag with the blue outline star 7 x 7 on a 3 px blue-and-white cord from a swivel under the front ring, 20 px ahead of the grip (clear of both heroes' bodies); upright and whole in every row, swinging by whole pixels with the shot, the pop of the next missile and the toss. In atlas_mark.png ONLY (the Host's ruling)
mark_rect_note: per angle row, per column: [x, y, w, h] of the mark in the cell (the 9 x 11 tag, or the 11 x 11 roundel) and mark_star = the top-left pixel of the star (7 x 7 on the tag, 9 x 9 on a roundel); atlas_mark.png holds the mark alone in the same layout

events.draw: the launcher comes up from the hip (arsenal.json equip 0)
events.screen_on: the sight comes on (equip 8): a power-up blip, the lens lights orange
events.ready: the act is over on this frame's last tick: can fire
events.anticipation: the 1-tick squash, on the shot's own tick (fire 0)
events.shot: the launch (fire 0): the missile leaves at `muzzle` (FX's), the flash at the mouth, the kick (no back-blast: the bell is at his chin)
events.remote_up: the remote comes up (fire 6): the antenna pops out of the sight, the lens goes green: he steers
events.click: the trigger on an empty tube (empty 0)
events.toss: the spent launcher leaves his hand (empty 6)
events.reveal: RENDER fires the reveal from this pose

normal_note: by plane: every colour paints one plane of the weapon (top, front, underside ...), turned with the row; silhouette pixels face out along the edge; the upright mark faces the viewer

holds.note: THE SET'S OWN CARRY per hero body pose (the Host 12.11: a hero's face is never covered by his weapon in any pose). While the king plays one of these body animations with this weapon, draw the weapon at `aim` (degrees, the body's hand aim replaced) and its hand point moved by `offset` [x, y] px; the frame's own aim delta and kick still add. His port carry (aim 25-40) puts a long weapon across his chin and mouth; a low hip carry at -20 keeps the face and the crown clear (picture: art/weapons/host/previews/king_carry_long_weapons.png). GUIDED (round 2): every weapon-bearing body pose of BOTH heroes was solved for 0 face px covered (the smallest move first; the fire poses stay level, aim 0) against every weapon frame that plays over it (scratch facecheck/solve, the ART C reviewer's face measure). The king's fire body hops 21 px (the shotgun's recoil pose): one offset per pose must keep the tube under his chin at the top of the hop, so his fire carry sits low (hip) the whole act; a per-frame carry is asked of RENDER (INTEGRATION_NOTES, `frames`). Ben-Gurion's reveal / victory holds the launcher up BESIDE his head.

muzzle_note: the tube's mouth on its axis, per row and column: the missile leaves here (fire 0). No back-blast is drawn (the fire carry holds the bell at his chin; critic 18.11) and FX adds none
reload_note: guided has no reload act in arsenal.json: its reload show is inside fire (ticks 26-40): the next missile pops in on a spring (columns pop, bounce, settle)

glow.note: the mouth flash's colours as drawn (gold, ivory core); the sight goes green while he steers

cells: the canopy flat on the floor
sprites.anchor: the cell's TOP-left at `at` (frame px; the sprite stands on the cell's bottom, centred)

catch.note: the weapon's side of the unarmed set's catch, on the same ticks and hand points as the shotgun's catch.json (the body is one builder's): frames 0-2 it comes down, 3 the catch (its grip lands on the hand), 3-4 what carried it lets go, 5-6 in the hands, 7-9 held up behind his head (layer back), the reveal from 9. Its carrier is the parachute: on the catch it folds, then lies on the floor.
